derived_from: the OWASP GenAI Crosswalk / LLM Top 10 / AI-BOM cross-check assessment

evidence_tiers.MEASURED_OPEN: Reproduced by a benchmark; a number exists and it is not yet at target.
evidence_tiers.MEASURED_CLOSED: Reproduced by a benchmark, fixed, and re-benchmarked to target.
evidence_tiers.UNMEASURED: Capability gap visible from code/contract review that the current benchmark corpus structurally cannot expose.
evidence_tiers.STRUCTURAL: Gap confirmed by source inspection; no benchmark has been built for it yet.

root_cause_classes.ARTIFACT: Findings dropped before reaching the report because an optional auxiliary layer of the pipeline raised and its exception was swallowed - a harness execution failure, not a detection-logic defect.
root_cause_classes.PARSER_GAP: No parser exists for the target language or construct.
root_cause_classes.ARCH_GAP: Structural shortfall: required stage does not exist as an independent stage.
root_cause_classes.SINK_GAP: Sink not modelled, or not validated as concrete.
root_cause_classes.RULE_GAP: Detection rule absent, or rules are not declarative/versioned.
root_cause_classes.TAINT_GAP: Taint propagation, interprocedural reach, or path reconstruction incomplete.
root_cause_classes.ALIAS_GAP: Receiver, alias, or object-field resolution missing.
root_cause_classes.SANITIZER_GAP: Sanitizer model absent or modelled for the wrong vulnerability class.
root_cause_classes.SCOPE_GAP: Scope/frame/binding resolution wrong, or analysis scope too narrow.
root_cause_classes.EVIDENCE_GAP: Finding or value produced but dropped, unlabelled, or mislabelled downstream.
root_cause_classes.VERSION_PARSE_GAP: Package version parsed incorrectly or its specifier retained.
root_cause_classes.MERGE_GAP: Advisory data overwritten instead of merged.
root_cause_classes.DISCOVERY_GAP: Package inventory inaccurate: invented or missing entries.
root_cause_classes.DATA_GAP: Intelligence is a static placeholder rather than a live feed, or the source is absent.
root_cause_classes.GRANULARITY_GAP: Analysis performed at a coarser granularity than required.
root_cause_classes.ENUM_GAP: Required status or type enumeration unimplemented.
root_cause_classes.STUB_GAP: Placeholder implementation standing in for the required pipeline.
root_cause_classes.RESOLUTION_GAP: Cannot resolve a symbol or constant to its concrete value.
root_cause_classes.WIRING_GAP: Component built and tested but never invoked.
root_cause_classes.CONTRACT_GAP: Test expectation and implementation contract conflict.
root_cause_classes.COVERAGE_GAP: Benchmark corpus does not cover the capability class.
root_cause_classes.SEED_TABLE_INVENTION: Compiled-in intelligence asserts a fact about an external authority (e.g. 'CISA lists this CVE') that the authority does not publish.
root_cause_classes.FILE_SCOPE_GAP: A rule has no file-scope exclusion, so it evaluates content in files that cannot contain the kind of secret or defect it looks for (lockfiles, generated manifests).
root_cause_classes.FRAMEWORK_SOURCE_GAP: A source that exists in the framework's routing or request API is not modelled, so request derived values never enter the taint graph.
root_cause_classes.ASSIGNMENT_SHAPE_GAP: The detector recognises one binding shape for a secret and misses the same secret bound through an index expression, an inline header dict, or a literal below the rule's length floor.
root_cause_classes.SCHEMA_ALIGNMENT_GAP: Producer and consumer agree on the concept but not on the field names or types, so data written by one side is invisible to the other.
root_cause_classes.EDITION_CONFORMANCE_GAP: An identifier is cited against a specification edition that does not contain it, or with a title belonging to a different entry in that edition.

gaps.title: EPSS is a static 8-CVE table, not a feed
gaps.problem: Prioritisation cites an `epss` field that is a hard-coded table covering 8 CVEs. Outside those 8 the value is absent yet is rendered with the same authority as real intelligence.
gaps.reference_tool: Exploit Prediction Scoring System (FIRST.org) via Grype / Dependency-Track
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Pulls the weekly EPSS CSV/JSON feed, indexes by CVE, stores the score with a fetch timestamp, and refreshes on a schedule.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE: `analysis/epss_intelligence_engine.py:12-21` held a literal table of 8 CVE->score pairs with no fetch, no timestamp and no refresh. AFTER: `analysis/live_intel_feeds.py` provides `EPSSFeed` (batched `?cve=A,B` queries, 24h disk cache at reports/.intel_feed_cache.json, timeout and TTL env-tunable) and `enrich_epss_intelligence(sbom, feed)` resolves live > cached snapshot > the SBOM's own value > seed table > absent, emitting `epss_provenance` / `epss_source` / `epss_as_of` / `epss_method`. `main.py` supplies `default_feed()`; live feeds default ON with an explicit operator opt-out (`RSECOPSX_LIVE_FEEDS=0`).
gaps.actual_gap: CLOSED. On the 80-CVE benchmark corpus EPSS resolution moved from P=1.0 / R=0.1013 / F1=0.1839 (10.0% coverage) offline to P=1.0 / R=1.0 / F1=1.0 (98.75%) live; the remaining 1.25% is the never-issued sentinel, which correctly resolves to NOT_AVAILABLE. Value fidelity against the reference moved from exact=0.0% (MAE 0.075839, max error 0.19233) to exact=100% (MAE 0.0). The offline figure is the substantive one: every seed-table score had drifted from FIRST.org, and none was attributed to a date.
gaps.implementation_location: analysis/live_intel_feeds.py (new: EPSSFeed/KEVFeed/FeedSet, cache, transport, config flags); analysis/epss_intelligence_engine.py (feed-aware enrich + derived summary); analysis/kev_intelligence_engine.py; analysis/vulnerability_age_engine.py (must not downgrade a live answer); main.py:_feeds default_feed() wiring + _apply_epss_kev_provenance_banner; reporting/{pdf_report,excel_report}.py payload-aware caption via analysis/intelligence_provenance.note_from_payload/provenance_pair
gaps.evidence: benchmark=intel-feeds-2026-10, analysis/benchmark_intel_feeds.py; ground truth fetched from the two authoritative feeds and written to reports/benchmark_intel_ground_truth.json BEFORE any product code ran, so the product is measured against a snapshot it could not have seen. Corpus 80 CVEs: 70 OSV-derived SCA CVEs + every compiled-in seed-table entry + a never-issued sentinel (CVE-2099-999999). Reports: reports/benchmark_intel_reconciliation.{json,md}. EPSS resolution offline P=1.0 R=0.1013 F1=0.1839 (8/80) -> live P=1.0 R=1.0 F1=1.0 (79/80); value fidelity offline exact=0.0% MAE=0.075839 max=0.19233 -> live exact=100% MAE=0.0. 73 `epss_bucket` and 11 `epss_priority` decisions move when the feed goes live - the reported impact of closing the gap. Provenance: offline claims LIVE_FEED 0 times, live-run provenance errors 0; RSECOPSX_LIVE_FEEDS=0 safety gate PASS (full report produced, zero LIVE_FEED claims, reason surfaced). Sentinel resolves to NOT_AVAILABLE on both paths - a miss never becomes a number. tests/test_v11_g001_g002_live_feeds.py 18/18 hermetic (local HTTP server serving the documented EPSS shape + pre-seeded dated cache; no test reaches the public internet). Suite 236 -> 254, 0 failed. SAST F1 1.0 and SCA CVE F1 1.0 unchanged; integrity 20/20; compile 156/0; PDF smoke PASS; E2E 13 findings, 0 removed.

gaps.title: KEV is ~9 hard-coded records, not the CISA catalog
gaps.problem: A `kev` field implies CISA known-exploited status. With ~9 records the platform will silently report `not in KEV` for the overwhelming majority of exploited CVEs — a false negative presented as a negative.
gaps.reference_tool: CISA KEV catalog, consumed by Trivy / Grype / Dependency-Track
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Fetches https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json, indexes by CVE, refreshes on the catalog cadence.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE: `analysis/kev_intelligence_engine.py:13-86` held ~9 literal records and `analysis/vulnerability_age_engine.py:9-12` a second, independent 7-CVE set that overwrote the same `kev_status` field after the KEV pass ran. AFTER: `KEVFeed` fetches the full CISA catalog JSON (1734 records at benchmark time) into the same shared cache, and `enrich_kev_intelligence(sbom, feed)` answers live-first while emitting `kev_source` / `kev_catalog_version` / `kev_as_of` / `kev_method`. The age engine now captures any upstream answer first and can only supply one when nothing upstream has spoken: a live answer is never overwritten nor relabelled, at package level or in the nested `vulnerability_intelligence` records that PDF, Excel and CycloneDX all render.
gaps.actual_gap: CLOSED. Against CISA catalog 2026.10.04 (1734 records) KEV determination is P=1.0 / R=1.0 / F1=1.0 offline and live on the benchmark corpus. The offline parity is the outcome of a defect the benchmark found: the seed table asserted `kev_status: True` for CVE-2024-3094, which CISA has never published (root_cause SEED_TABLE_INVENTION), with an invented `kev_added_date` / `due_date` in CISA's own field format. That entry was withdrawn from both seed sets; the CVE keeps its disclosure date, CVSS 10.0 and EPSS score, so only the false attribution is withdrawn.
gaps.implementation_location: analysis/live_intel_feeds.py (KEVFeed); analysis/kev_intelligence_engine.py (feed-aware enrich + derived summary + seed-set correction); analysis/vulnerability_age_engine.py (2 write sites + summary, upstream capture via known_provenance); main.py wiring; analysis/intelligence_provenance.py (intelligence_note/provenance_pair/note_from_payload/known_provenance)
gaps.evidence: benchmark=intel-feeds-2026-10, analysis/benchmark_intel_feeds.py; ground truth fetched from the two authoritative feeds and written to reports/benchmark_intel_ground_truth.json BEFORE any product code ran, so the product is measured against a snapshot it could not have seen. Corpus 80 CVEs: 70 OSV-derived SCA CVEs + every compiled-in seed-table entry + a never-issued sentinel (CVE-2099-999999). Reports: reports/benchmark_intel_reconciliation.{json,md}. KEV determination offline P=1.0 R=1.0 F1=1.0, TN=72 -> live P=1.0 R=1.0 F1=1.0, TN=72, against the 1734-record catalog. The first run reported P=0.8889 (1 FP, root_cause SEED_TABLE_INVENTION): CVE-2024-3094, confirmed absent by a second independent direct fetch of the CISA feed document - CISA published an *alert* on 2024-03-29, not a KEV entry, and KEV requires reliable evidence of in-the-wild exploitation. `kev_status` moves True -> False for that one identifier when the feed goes live; no other KEV decision moves. A live miss is labelled LIVE_FEED (the whole catalog was consulted) while an offline miss stays STATIC_REFERENCE - the two never collapse into each other. An item with no identifier gets NOT_AVAILABLE, never LIVE_FEED. Order hazard closed and pinned: with a live answer present the age pass cannot overwrite or relabel it (test_14 reproduces the package and nested-record paths). Suite 236 -> 254, 0 failed; integrity 20/20; compile 156/0; PDF smoke PASS; SCA CVE F1 1.0.

gaps.title: Static EPSS/KEV must be labelled STATIC_REFERENCE until live
gaps.problem: Until G-001/G-002 land, any report that renders these fields as intelligence is making a claim the data does not support.
gaps.reference_tool: Snyk / Dependency-Track
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Omits the field entirely when the feed is unavailable rather than rendering a stale or placeholder value.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE: the engines wrote `epss_method` / `kev_method` but no reporter read them, and `analysis/vulnerability_age_engine.py` wrote `kev_status` / `actively_exploited` with no provenance field at all. PDF, Excel, VEX and CycloneDX all rendered `EPSS 0.975` and `KEV No` as bare values, so a reader could not distinguish an 8-row offline table from a live feed. AFTER: `analysis/intelligence_provenance.py` defines the token vocabulary; all three engines emit `epss_provenance` / `kev_provenance`; PDF, Excel, VEX and CycloneDX render it; `main.py:_apply_epss_kev_provenance_banner` publishes `metadata.epss_kev_provenance` with `live_feeds_wired: false`.
gaps.actual_gap: CLOSED. Every EPSS/KEV value now carries `STATIC_REFERENCE` (or `NOT_AVAILABLE` for an absent score) on every report surface, including the `kev_status: False` branch, which is the case where the bare boolean was most misleading. The underlying data gap (G-001/G-002) is untouched and remains P0.
gaps.implementation_location: analysis/intelligence_provenance.py (new, token vocabulary); analysis/epss_intelligence_engine.py; analysis/kev_intelligence_engine.py; analysis/vulnerability_age_engine.py (2 write sites); main.py:_apply_epss_kev_provenance_banner + main.py:_build_dependency_reporting_views; reporting/pdf_report.py:_sbom_section; reporting/excel_report.py:_static_intel_note (SBOM / SCA Findings / Exploitable CVEs sheets); reporting/vex_export.py:_statement; reporting/cyclonedx_export.py:_vulnerability
gaps.evidence: tests/test_v11_g003_static_reference_labelling.py 29/29: provenance on every write site, `kev_status False` still labelled, value/bucket/priority invariance (scores, buckets, P0/P3 priorities and summary counts byte-identical before and after), report-surface rendering for PDF/Excel/VEX/CycloneDX, JSON payload views (`dependency_risk_register`, `top_cves`, `reachable_vulnerable_packages`, `not_observed_vulnerable_packages`), and a negative control asserting no producer claims LIVE_FEED. End-to-end proof: `generate_pdf_report` -> pdftotext/pypdf extract 'EPSS / KEV provenance: STATIC_REFERENCE ... not from the live FIRST.org EPSS API' directly beneath the table still showing 0.975. Suite 207 -> 236, 0 failed; SAST F1 1.0 and SCA CVE F1 1.0 unchanged; integrity 20/20; PDF smoke PASS.

gaps.title: `aibom_abom_correlation` built, tested, never invoked
gaps.problem: The SBOM↔AI-BOM↔ABOM↔CBOM correlation capability — a declared research differentiator — never runs during a scan, so no product output contains it.
gaps.reference_tool: No mainstream tool does cross-BOM correlation (this is the differentiator).
gaps.how_reference_does_it: n/a — no mainstream equivalent; nearest are Dependency-Track's asset/programme linkage.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE: `scanner/aibom_abom_correlation.py` (~416 L, 5 test files) was never imported by `main.py`, so no product output contained it. AFTER: `main.py` imports `correlate` as `correlate_aibom_abom` and runs it as the phase `AI-BOM <-> ABOM correlation` immediately after the BOM payload is assembled, publishing `payload["bom_correlation"]` (the relationship list) and `payload["bom_correlation_summary"]` (status, error, relationships, by_relationship_type, abom_items, aibom_items, detection=CROSS_BOM_CORRELATION_V1). The call is wrapped so an engine failure degrades to an empty list recorded as status=DEGRADED with the exception text, never as a silent 'no relationships exist'.
gaps.actual_gap: CLOSED for the gap as written - the capability is invoked on every scan and its output ships in the report. Measured on the AI/LLM corpus: status CORRELATED, abom_items=3, aibom_items=91, relationships=0. That zero is correct for these inputs (the ABOM holds three `Tool` components and no Agent component) but it also exposes a second, separate defect that is NOT closed here: the MODEL/PROVIDED_BY legs cannot fire at all. Registered as G-039.
gaps.implementation_location: main.py - `from scanner.aibom_abom_correlation import correlate as correlate_aibom_abom` (import) and the `AI-BOM <-> ABOM correlation` step immediately after `payload["abom"] = abom`
gaps.evidence: grep: `main.py` now imports and calls `correlate_aibom_abom(`; source contract asserted by tests/test_v11_p0_owasp_aibom_conformance.py::test_20/21/22. E2E log phase `AI-BOM <-> ABOM correlation` prints `BOM correlation: 0 relationship(s) | status: CORRELATED`. Payload inspection: bom_correlation_summary = {status: CORRELATED, error: "", relationships: 0, by_relationship_type: {}, abom_items: 3, aibom_items: 91, detection: CROSS_BOM_CORRELATION_V1}. Identity gating still holds: test_23 asserts a declared `GPT-5` agent links to GPT-5 and never to CLAUDE-X, and emits a PROVIDED_BY edge only for a model that declares a provider that actually exists in the same aibom. Regression: full suite 291/0, integrity 20/20, compile 158/0, E2E 14->13, GenAI benchmark identical.

gaps.title: Benchmark classes B, C, D unmeasured — 100% does not generalise
gaps.problem: The only measured SAST/SCA corpora are class A (controlled synthetic). A perfect class-A score proves the previously-found defects are gone; it says nothing about OWASP-style applications, real-world repositories, or AI/LLM code.
gaps.reference_tool: OWASP Benchmark, DVWA, Juice Shop, SecurityShepherd; project corpora used by Semgrep/CodeQL CI suites
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Runs against curated applications with published expected results, plus seeded real-world repos, and reports per-category recall.
gaps.current_behavior: `analysis/benchmark_sast_corpus.py` measures 13 vulns + 6 controls, all hand-authored. `analysis/benchmark_sca_corpus.py` measures 11 packages / 70 CVEs, all hand-authored.
gaps.actual_gap: Classes B (OWASP apps), C (real-world OSS), D (AI/LLM corpus) have no ground truth and have never been run.
gaps.implementation_location: analysis/benchmark_sast_corpus.py (extend), analysis/benchmark_sca_corpus.py (extend); new corpora under a fixture root
gaps.evidence: enterprise_capability_matrix.md §1 note: 'class B and class C are still not measured, so 100% here does not generalise'.

gaps.title: Discovery precision 61.1% — 7 synthesised transitive deps with unknown versions
gaps.problem: R-SecOpsX emits 18 packages where 11 are declared. The 7 extras are invented from a hardcoded table with `version: unknown`, `direct: False`. They are unverifiable claims inside a deliverable SBOM.
gaps.reference_tool: Trivy (91.7%), Grype (100.0%) on the same corpus
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Reads the lockfile's resolved graph (npm lock, poetry.lock, etc.) so transitive edges come from real resolution data, never from a hardcoded table.
gaps.current_behavior: `scanner/sbom.py` `_add_transitive` synthesises certifi, jinja2, path-to-regexp, qs, sqlparse, urllib3, werkzeug. They never match a CVE, so CVE precision stays 100%.
gaps.actual_gap: Discovery F1 75.9% vs Grype 100%. Invented inventory entries in a signed deliverable.
gaps.implementation_location: scanner/sbom.py `_add_transitive`
gaps.evidence: reports/benchmark_reconciliation_sca.md: R-SecOpsX pkgs 18, precision 61.1%; extras listed by name.

gaps.title: Reachability is package-level; §10 function granularity and type enum absent
gaps.problem: The product is described as reachability-aware. It can only say whether an *import* of a vulnerable package appears — not whether the vulnerable function is on a call path.
gaps.reference_tool: Semgrep Supply Chain (NATIVE function-level), Trivy reachability (PARTIAL)
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Resolves the advisory's affected symbol, indexes the project's call graph, and reports whether that symbol is reachable; emits a reachability type (DIRECT/INDIRECT/...).
gaps.current_behavior: `scanner/reachability.py:372` regex-extracts imports, matches to SBOM, emits REACHABLE/UNREACHABLE/UNKNOWN at `:273,343` with confidence 0.85/0.65/0.30.
gaps.actual_gap: No `vulnerable_function`, no `call_path`, no DIRECT/INDIRECT/TRANSITIVE/CALL_FLOW/DATA_FLOW/CONFIGURATION/RUNTIME enum.
gaps.implementation_location: scanner/reachability.py:227,238,250,273,343,372; §10 schema fields
gaps.evidence: enterprise_capability_matrix.md §4; 'Never infer from install alone' is correctly implemented and must be preserved.

gaps.how_reference_does_it: Evaluates a declarative policy over scored inputs (severity, exploitability, exposure, criticality, control coverage) and returns a decision with provenance.

gaps.title: No compensating-controls model; no inherent vs residual risk
gaps.problem: Findings carry no notion that a control may reduce residual risk, so all findings of a severity are treated identically regardless of compensating controls.
gaps.reference_tool: Dependency-Track (risk score with control context); NIST 800-30 style inherent/residual modelling
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Stores controls against assets/services, applies them as a multiplier/offset to inherent risk, and reports both values with provenance.
gaps.current_behavior: Prose strings only: `sast.py:224`, `legacy_protocol_engine.py:88`.
gaps.actual_gap: No controls module; §16 unmet; inherent vs residual risk not distinguished.

gaps.title: CBOM does not resolve mode, key size, or curve
gaps.problem: CBOM reports 'AES present' without saying whether it is GCM or ECB, and 'RSA present' without key size — so a weak-configuration finding is impossible to make.
gaps.reference_tool: Microsoft SBOM-Tool / Syft crypto inventory; OWASP crypto guidance
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Resolves the algorithm call's arguments (mode constant, key-size constant) through symbol/constant propagation, and records mode+size+padding on the crypto element.
gaps.current_behavior: `cbom.py:70` AES rule text literally reads 'Verify AES mode is GCM/CTR'; `cbom.py:84` RSA reads 'Verify RSA key size ≥2048'. Regex over literals only.
gaps.actual_gap: Mode, key size, curve, padding, protocol all unmet (§21).
gaps.implementation_location: scanner/cbom.py:70,84,118
gaps.evidence: enterprise_capability_matrix.md §6.

gaps.title: No non-Python parser — tree-sitter absent repo-wide
gaps.problem: Every non-Python language is analysed by regex + brace matching. Accepted file extensions (.kt .scala .rb .cs .cpp .c .h .vb) have no parser, so inclusion in SCANNABLE_EXT must not be read as support.
gaps.reference_tool: Semgrep, CodeQL (NATIVE parsers for all supported languages)
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Embeds a real grammar per language (tree-sitter for Semgrep) and produces a CST/AST consumed by shared data-flow passes.
gaps.current_behavior: Python uses `ast` (`taint_engine.py:96`). Repo grep for tree-sitter/javalang = 0. `sast.py:42` SCANNABLE_EXT lists 7 further extensions.
gaps.actual_gap: 9 of 12 listed languages are PATTERN_ONLY; none of Rust/PowerShell supported.
gaps.implementation_location: new parser module; scanner/taint_engine.py:96; scanner/sast.py:42
gaps.evidence: enterprise_capability_matrix.md §8 language coverage matrix.

gaps.title: AI/LLM corpus: 0/6 path-traversal and code-write sinks reported
gaps.problem: Across the OWASP GenAI Red Team Lab the product reported no path_traversal and no code_injection finding at all, on six pre-registered positives where an HTTP request value reaches `open()`, `kv.persist()` or a `.py` write with no sanitisation between.
gaps.reference_tool: Semgrep (python.flask.security.audit.path-traversal-via-param, path-traversal-with-containment) and CodeQL (py/path-injection) both cover FastAPI `:path` route parameters and Flask request-derived paths.
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Models framework routing: a `{name:path}` converter or `request.args[...]` becomes a source, `open`/`write` become sinks, and containment is checked by whether a realpath/basename guard dominates the sink.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE: `scanner/taint_engine.py` had no route-parameter source, so a FastAPI `/{bucket}/{object:path}` or Flask `/<path:fname>` binding never entered the taint graph; `visit_Assign` only recognised a source that *was* the whole RHS, so `data = request.get_json(...) or {}` left `data` untainted; the taint kill ran unconditionally on every Constant assignment, so `remainder = ""` in a sibling `else:` declassified a value an `if:` branch had just derived from the request; `DANGEROUS_SINKS` had no `persist`, so `kv.persist(persist_path=path)` and `storage_context.persist(persist_dir=...)` were invisible; `self.headers`/`self.rfile.read` on a `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` were not sources; and a callee's parameters were never seeded from a caller, so `_peek(remainder)` -> `open(path, 'r')` and `handle_document_reader(path)` -> `open(resolved, 'r')` were unreachable. AFTER: `_route_param_map()` seeds only the names that literally appear in the decorator's route template, handling both spellings (`{name:converter}` and `<converter:name>`); `visit_Assign` propagates taint from a source nested anywhere in the RHS; the constant kill is block-scoped through `_mark_tainted`/`_kill_overwrites`/`_block_path`, so a sibling `else:` no longer declassifies while a same-block assignment still does; `persist` is a `path_traversal` sink; `visit_With` records write-mode file handles and `visit_Call` reports a tainted `.write()`/`.writelines()` whose registered open target contains `.py` as `code_injection`; `self.headers`/`self.rfile.read` are sources; and `_seed_callee()` seeds same-file formal parameters from *request-derived* arguments only, with caller locals hidden by `_stop_at`, a re-entrancy guard and a depth cap of 6.
gaps.actual_gap: CLOSED. Four structural causes, all measured against the pre-registered ground truth (root causes: FRAMEWORK_SOURCE_GAP route parameters and http.server request surfaces; TAINT_GAP nested-source assignment and same-file call seeding; SINK_GAP `persist` and the module write; SCOPE_GAP block-insensitive taint kill; plus EVIDENCE_GAP in the EVIDEX sink catalogue, registered as G-045). RESIDUAL 1 (deliberate, recorded under `not_proposed`): `os.getenv`/`sys.argv`/`input()` still taint inside their own function but are NOT propagated across a function boundary. Propagating them was the first implementation of this gap and it produced three command-injection findings on `run_cmd(f'cd "{SANDBOX_DIR}" && docker build ...')` plus negative-control violation NC-03 on this corpus; cross-function seeding is therefore restricted to request-derived sources. RESIDUAL 2: the fix required hand-editing a second sink list in `core/analyzer.py` (`_EVIDEX_SINK_ALIASES`), which is not derived from the taint engine's sink map - G-045.
gaps.implementation_location: scanner/taint_engine.py - `TAINT_SOURCES` (self.headers, self.rfile.read), `DANGEROUS_SINKS` (persist), `_route_param_map`, `_function_map`, `_formal_params`, `_ROUTE_PARAM_RE`, `_NETWORK_SOURCE_TOKENS`/`_network_source`/`_network_taint`, `_mark_tainted`/`_kill_overwrites`/`_block_path`/`_visit_body` and the block visitors, `visit_Assign` nested-source branch, `visit_FunctionDef` route seeding, `visit_With`/`visit_Call` (write handles, code_injection, `_seed_callee`), `_record` dedupe, `_python_ast_findings` (passing both maps); core/analyzer.py - `_EVIDEX_SINK_ALIASES["file"] += ".persist("` and `_EVIDEX_SINK_ALIASES["code"] += ".write(", ".writelines("` (G-045 records that this coupling is manual).
gaps.evidence: BEFORE: reports/benchmark_reconciliation_genai.{json,md} benchmark ai-llm-corpus-genai-2026-10 against reports/ground_truth_genai.json (authored before the scan) -> PATH_TRAVERSAL 0/5 = 0.0000, CODE_INJECTION 0/1 = 0.0000, overall pre-registered recall 5/11 = 0.4545, precision 0.9412, credential recall 16/29 = 0.5517, negative-control violations 0/6, findings 56. AFTER (same ground truth, same command, distinct scan dir): PATH_TRAVERSAL 5/5 = 1.0000 (GT-01..GT-05 matched at lines 37/332/357/305/74), CODE_INJECTION 1/1 = 1.0000 (GT-06 at line 402), HARDCODED_CREDENTIAL 5/5, overall pre-registered recall 11/11 = 1.0000, precision 0.9565 (TP 22 / FP 1 - the single FP is unchanged and CONTEXT_MISCLASSIFIED), credential recall 16/29 = 0.5517 unchanged, negative-control violations 0/6 (an intermediate implementation regressed NC-03 to 1/6 and that was the trigger for the network-only seeding bound), findings 56 -> 68. Tests: tests/test_v11_g035_framework_taint.py, 23 tests pinning GT-01..GT-06, the route-template negative control, both kill controls, source-nested-in-BoolOp and -in-cast, callee seeding (positional and keyword), caller-locals isolation, recursion termination, the operator-source negative control, and EVIDEX accept/accept/reject. Regression: full suite 319 passed / 0 failed (296 before this change, 255 before this programme), compile 158/0, integrity 20/20 PASS, SAST F1 1.0 with TP/FP/FN/TN 13/0/0/6, SCA pkg F1 0.7586 and CVE F1 1.0 unchanged, threat-intel offline clean and live P=R=F1=1.0, E2E fixture 14 -> 13 with 7 unchanged, GenAI scan EXIT 0.

gaps.title: Credential rule fires inside lockfiles (42/54 FPs) and misses enforcement sites
gaps.problem: Two opposite failures in one rule. It evaluates npm lockfiles, where integrity hashes, `engines.node` ranges and dependency names are matched as credentials; and it misses the sites that actually make a secret a secret - the `if token != "..."` authorization comparisons that gate every route.
gaps.reference_tool: gitleaks and TruffleHog: both carry per-path allow-lists for lockfiles/manifests, and detect a secret by its entropy plus a known-provider or auth-context pattern rather than by variable name alone.
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Rule-level path filtering (`allowlist.paths`) so lockfiles are skipped outright, plus detection rules that require the literal to sit in an authentication context.

The same rule never fired on `if token != "sk-mock-key"` in five mock servers, `if api_key != "foobar"` (s3.py) or `if api_key != "bar"` (pinecone.py) - the seven comparisons that actually return 401.

gaps.how_reference_does_it: Reports only when a flow from an untrusted source reaches the command argument; the sink alone is not sufficient evidence.

gaps.actual_gap: Command-injection precision 0/11. Negative-control violation rate 3/6 = 0.5000 - the rule fires on an f-string alone, which is precisely the absence-to-positive-claim failure the programme forbids.
gaps.implementation_location: scanner/sast.py: _gate_shell_sink_findings() with SHELL_SINK_RULE_IDS and SHELL_SINK_TAINT_WINDOW, applied in scan_directory._scan() immediately after taint_analyze() returns, guarded by taint_ok. (CORRECTED: the original entry said scanner/taint_engine.py, but SUBPROCESS_SHELL_TRUE and OS_SYSTEM are defined in scanner/sast.py REGEX_RULES at lines ~195-196 and are produced by the regex loop, not by the taint engine.)

TRUE POSITIVES RETAINED, so this is a precision fix and not a detection removal: SAST benchmark command_injection 5/5 recall 1.0 (GT-02, GT-03, GT-07, GT-11, GT-13) and E2E still reports Vuln.java:6, app.py:13, index.php:5, main.go:10, server.js:6. gaps.title: 13 of 29 credential sites undetected - os.environ[...] bindings and sub-8-character literals
gaps.problem: After G-036 the mechanically enumerated credential inventory is 29 sites and 16 are found. The 13 misses have two distinct causes. Ten are `os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "sk-mock-key"`, where an index expression sits between the credential name and the `=`, so `GENERIC_API_KEY_PASSWORD`'s `\s*[:=]` cannot bridge it. Three are 3-character literals - `API_KEY = "bar"`, `PINECONE_API_KEY = "bar"` twice - that sit under the 8-character floor shared by `GENERIC_API_KEY_PASSWORD` `{8,}` and `_looks_like_secret_value`'s `len(x)<8` rejection, even though `bar` is the enforced secret that returns 401 at mocks/pinecone.py:40. Both are binding/length rules, not evidence rules: the secret is present in the file either way.
gaps.reference_tool: gitleaks and TruffleHog match on value signatures and per-provider rules rather than on how the value is bound, and each rule declares its own minimum length instead of sharing one global floor.
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Detects the literal by its shape or provider pattern independent of the surrounding binding, and lets a short shared secret be covered by a provider rule with a low minimum.
gaps.current_behavior: scanner/sast.py GENERIC_API_KEY_PASSWORD pattern `(?:api[_-]?key|...)\s*[:=]\s*["'][A-Za-z0-9@#$%^&+=!_.\-/]{8,}["']`; scanner/secret_intelligence.py _looks_like_secret_value returns False for any value shorter than 8 characters.
gaps.actual_gap: Credential recall 16/29 = 0.5517. 10 os.environ index bindings and 3 short enforced literals are invisible to every credential rule in the product.
gaps.implementation_location: scanner/sast.py GENERIC_API_KEY_PASSWORD (accept an index or attribute expression before the `=`); scanner/secret_intelligence.py _scan_source_assignments and _looks_like_secret_value (per-rule minimum length rather than one global 8-character floor), keeping _is_placeholder and entropy checks intact so lowering the floor does not import placeholder noise

gaps.problem: G-004 wired `correlate()` into the scan, which made a second defect observable: the MODEL->PROVIDED_BY leg is structurally unreachable. `_is_model` requires `model_id` plus `model_name`/`entity_type==MODEL`/`asset_type==MODEL`; `_is_provider` requires `provider_id` plus `provider_name`/`entity_type==PROVIDER`/`asset_type==PROVIDER`. `scanner/aibom.py` never writes any of those six keys - it writes `component_id`, a free-text `provider` label and `model_value`/`model_reference`/`model_usages` for resolved model *usages* on a component.
gaps.reference_tool: No mainstream tool performs cross-BOM correlation; the nearest contract examples are the CycloneDX AI/BOM component identity and Dependency-Track's asset linkage.
gaps.how_reference_does_it: n/a - the nearest practice is to give each entity a stable identifier in the producing document and have consumers join on that identifier rather than on display text.
gaps.current_behavior: E2E on the AI/LLM corpus: 91 AI-BOM items, of which 0 carry `model_id` and 0 carry `provider_id`; 1 resolves a `model_value` (`nomic-embed-text`). 3 ABOM items, of which 0 are Agent components (all three are `component: "Tool"` with a valid `component_id`). Result: `relationships: 0`, `status: CORRELATED`. The AGENT leg is aligned - `scanner/abom.py` does emit `component: "Agent"` for CrewAI agents, so that leg would fire on a corpus containing one.
gaps.actual_gap: MEASURED OPEN: 0 of 91 AI-BOM items are selectable as a model or a provider, so the MODEL->PROVIDED_BY half of the capability can never produce an edge regardless of input. gaps.implementation_location: scanner/aibom.py - emit model entities with `model_id`/`model_name` and provider entities with `provider_id`/`provider_name` for resolved model usages, OR scanner/aibom_abom_correlation.py `_is_model`/`_is_provider` if the component record is chosen as the identity. Whichever side is chosen, `_model_satisfies_reference` and `_agent_declared_model_reference` must join on the same field. Do NOT join on the free-text `provider` label: the corpus contains `provider: "OpenAI"` on an item whose `base_url=OLLAMA_BASE_URL` serves `nomic-embed-text`, so provider-label joining would manufacture a false PROVIDED_BY edge.

gaps.title: EVIDEX sink catalogue is a second, hand-maintained sink list
gaps.problem: `core/analyzer.py::_EVIDEX_VULN_TO_SINK` and `_EVIDEX_SINK_ALIASES` decide whether a finding's evidence contains a sink consistent with its `vuln_type`. When `enrich_finding()` sees `evidence_valid is False` it returns `{}` and the finding is silently dropped before the report, the risk score, the attack graph and the release decision. That catalogue is maintained by hand and is not derived from `scanner/taint_engine.py::DANGEROUS_SINKS`, so learning a new sink in the engine has no mechanical path to the validator.
gaps.reference_tool: CodeQL and Semgrep have one sink definition per query/rule; the rule that fires IS the rule that validates, so a new sink cannot be detected and rejected by the same codebase in the same release.
gaps.how_reference_does_it: A sink is declared once in the query (CodeQL `class FileSystemWriteAccess`, Semgrep `pattern-sources`/`pattern-sinks`) and every downstream stage - path reconstruction, sanitiser matching, message rendering - reads that single declaration.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE this phase: `storage_context.persist(...)`, `kv.persist(persist_path=...)` and `fh.write(payload)` were reported by the taint engine, then rejected by EVIDEX (`sink_present = False` -> `sink_valid = False` -> `evidence_valid = False`) and dropped at `enrich_finding()`, so the engine's own measurements (direct `analyze_file`) and the final report disagreed. AFTER: the aliases contain `.persist(` (file) and `.write(`, `.writelines(` (code), and the three findings survive. The disagreement is fixed; the coupling is still manual.
gaps.actual_gap: No test asserts that every sink in `DANGEROUS_SINKS` has a matching EVIDEX alias, so the next sink added to the engine will silently lose its findings at report time. The failure mode is invisible: the engine reports, `scan_directory` returns, and `enrich_finding` returns `{}` without logging.  COST XS: one test plus a log line. The alternative - deriving the aliases from `DANGEROUS_SINKS` automatically - is a real refactor of EVIDEX and would need its own benchmark, and is not proposed until the manual test has fired once.  REGRESSION RISK LOW: very low; the test and the log line change no decision path. Widening the alias list itself was the risky part and it is already guarded by test_evidex_still_rejects_code_injection_without_a_sink.
gaps.implementation_location: tests/test_v11_g035_framework_taint.py (add a catalogue-coupling test); core/analyzer.py::_EVIDEX_SINK_ALIASES, _EVIDEX_VULN_TO_SINK, enrich_finding
gaps.evidence: Reproduced before the alias fix: direct `taint_engine.analyze_file` on sandboxes/agentic_local_llamaindex/app/server.py returned 5 findings (L305/L332/L340/L357/L402) while `enrich_finding` returned `{}` for L305, L357 and L402 - all three for `sink_present = False`. gaps.title: 44 of 68 AI/LLM findings sit outside the three scored categories (UNEVALUATED)
gaps.problem: reports/ground_truth_genai.json pre-registers 11 positives and 6 negative controls over three categories only: PATH_TRAVERSAL, CODE_INJECTION and HARDCODED_CREDENTIAL. The current scan emits 68 findings of which 44 fall outside those categories - LLM supply-chain, API abuse, prompt-injection, rate-limit and secret-intelligence rows. The benchmark marks them UNEVALUATED, so they contribute to neither TP nor FP. Recall 11/11 = 1.0 and precision 0.9565 are therefore true statements about the scored subset and say nothing about 65% of what the product reported.
gaps.reference_tool: OWASP Benchmark (Java) scores 11 test categories with 2740 true-positive and true-negative cases; Semgrep's `semgrep --config p/ci` results are scored per rule against a labelled PR corpus. Both score the whole output, not a subset of it.
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Ground truth is authored as the full expected output for the corpus (every TP and every TN), so precision is measured on every emitted finding rather than on the findings that happen to be pre-registered.
gaps.current_behavior: `analysis/benchmark_genai_corpus.py` reconciles by category and computes precision over findings that fall in a scored category; everything else is `UNEVALUATED` and is reported as a count only. The count grew 38 -> 44 this phase because the new findings (s3.py L27/L32, llamaindex L340, and the EVIDEX-returned rows) include non-GT categories.
gaps.actual_gap: No ground truth exists for the LLM supply-chain, prompt-injection, API-abuse, rate-limit or secret-intelligence categories on this corpus, so their precision and recall are unknown. Reporting a headline precision of 0.9565 without the 44-row caveat overstates what has been measured.  COST M: authoring ground truth is the expensive part; roughly one working day split across two sessions because the truth must be written before the scan it is compared against. A first pass over the four largest unscored categories (llm_supply_chain, llm_prompt_injection, api_abuse, hardcoded_secret-from-env) would add ~10-15 positives and their negative controls, reusing the existing ±3-line reconciliation.  REGRESSION RISK MED: none on the engine; on the report, adding categories changes the denominator, so the published precision moves in both directions. That is the point of closing it, but it means the current 0.9565 must never be compared with a future number computed on the extended ground truth.

gaps.title: Translation catalogues and seed datasets are read as deployable configuration credentials
gaps.problem: A generic key/value parser ran over every `.json`/`.yml` in the target and reported any key whose name looks credential-shaped as a hardcoded configuration credential. In a translation catalogue the key is a UI label (`MANDATORY_PASSWORD`) and the value is a translated sentence; in a seed dataset it is a demo row. Neither exists in the running system, but each consumed a finding slot, dominated every aggregate, and made the report unreadable for a real codebase.
gaps.reference_tool: GitLeaks / TruffleHog path and entropy context
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Both gate credential-shaped matches behind file-class heuristics (repository fixtures, generated files, locale bundles) and behind value-entropy/signature checks, so a label without credential-like material is not reported as a secret.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE (Juice Shop): 1188 of 1290 findings (92.1%) were CONFIG_CONTEXTUAL_CREDENTIAL emitted as `key=[REDACTED]` - frontend/src/assets/i18n/*.json 993, data/static/i18n/*.json 172, data/static/users.yml 24, config/fbctf.yml 10 - i.e. 77.6% of all findings were frontend translation JSON, 96.6% were Low severity and only 20 findings (1.6%) sat in real application source. `_is_nonproduction_context()` covered test/docs/example/fixture directories but not locale bundles or seed datasets. AFTER: findings 1290 -> 102 (-1188, -92.1%), Low 1246 -> 58, and the leading directories are now real code - config/fbctf.yml 10, server.ts 9, .github/workflows/ci.yml 9, frontend/src/app 7, terraform/networking.tf 5, infrastructure/terraform/networking.tf 5.
gaps.actual_gap: CLOSED, and the scope is deliberately narrow. `_is_translated_text_or_seed_dataset()` withholds ONLY CONFIG_CONTEXTUAL_CREDENTIAL - the key/value interpretation - for path segments in {i18n, locale, locales, translations, l10n} or a `data|datasets|fixtures|seeds` parent followed by a `static|seed|seeds|fixture|fixtures` child. Known-signature, PEM, URI, JWT and high-entropy detection still run on those files. Control test: identical content at config/app.json and data/users.yml still reports CONFIG_CONTEXTUAL_CREDENTIAL, and a PEM inside an i18n catalogue still reports PEM_PRIVATE_KEY, so the guard cannot pass by the rule having been disabled outright. gaps.title: rule_telemetry and quality_state are emitted but never populated with per-rule outcomes
gaps.problem: The report ships `rule_telemetry` and a per-finding `quality_state`, which a consumer reads as calibrated evidence. The fields exist, are labelled, and assert nothing.
gaps.reference_tool: Semgrep `--metrics` triage / CodeQL rule precision badges / SonarQube rule SQ rating
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Each publishes a per-rule precision/recall figure derived from an adjudicated finding set (user triage, a labelled benchmark corpus, or both), and updates it as outcomes accumulate.
gaps.current_behavior: The suite-level benchmarks (SAST F1 1.0, GenAI precision 0.9565 / recall 1.0) compute and publish correctness for the whole run, but nothing writes a per-rule outcome back into rule_telemetry or quality_state, so no rule in the artifact carries a measured precision. quality_state is populated by the evidence/validation layer with NOT_ASSESSED when nothing adjudicated it - an honest default, but it is reported in the same structure as an assessment.
gaps.actual_gap: OPEN, STRUCTURAL. Confirmed by source inspection of the emitted artifact; no benchmark corpus exists that labels findings at the granularity of an individual rule, so a per-rule figure cannot be produced honestly today. Deliberately not faked: inventing a precision from suite-level numbers, or marking findings assessed on the strength of a detection pattern, would put an unearned claim in the report.

gaps.title: Dependency-derived OWASP categories (A06) can never appear in the OWASP summary
gaps.problem: A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components is by definition about dependencies, yet both OWASP aggregates are built by iterating `findings[]` and inferring a label per finding. A report holding three vulnerable packages therefore cannot emit A06 however many CVEs the SBOM carries, so the compliance view under-reports the category the SBOM is evidence for.
gaps.reference_tool: OWASP Dependency-Check / Grype / Dependency-Track OWASP Top 10 aggregation
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Aggregates findings AND dependency advisories into the Top 10, because A06 is satisfied by package evidence rather than by a source-level finding.
gaps.current_behavior: BEFORE and AFTER this cycle: Juice Shop clean_report.json has metadata.vulnerable_packages=3 while top-level `owasp` keys are A01, A02, A03, A04, A05, A07, A08, A10, API4, LLM02 - A06 absent - and framework_mapping_summary.by_owasp is absent-free for the same reason. The two aggregates agree with each other and with `findings[]`, so this is not the staleness defect tracked in G-047; it is a scope defect that existed before and after it.
gaps.actual_gap: OPEN, STRUCTURAL. Confirmed by source inspection: core/analyzer.py::_build_owasp_summary loops findings and calls _infer_owasp_value per finding; no SBOM input reaches it. Not implemented this cycle: emitting A06 from SBOM evidence is a new compliance claim, so it needs an authoritative mapping source, a stated provenance for it, and a benchmark assertion - not an opportunistic addition made while fixing an unrelated consistency defect.
gaps.implementation_location: core/analyzer.py::_build_owasp_summary (currently findings-only) and the call site in build_report_payload; would need SBOM/vulnerable_packages passed through, plus framework_mapping_summary.by_owasp kept in step

gaps.title: No raw-to-final finding reconciliation: dedupe merges are counted nowhere
gaps.problem: A reader who wants to know why a corpus went from N raw findings to M written findings cannot answer from the artifact. The transcript prints the raw population and one subtraction, metadata records the post-dedupe population, and the dedupe merge count exists in neither. `dedup_ratio` looks like the missing term but its recorded semantics are `SAST_ROOT_FINDINGS_DIVIDED_BY_SAST_OCCURRENCES`, so it cannot be used to recover it.
gaps.reference_tool: Trivy `--list-all-packages` + summary counters, Semgrep `--json` metrics block, CodeQL `runs[].invocations[].executionSuccessful` / `partialSuccesses`
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Emit a small stage ledger (scanned / filtered / merged / reported) alongside the result so the printed totals add up without the reader having to infer a step.
gaps.current_behavior: Juice Shop, after G-047/G-048: the transcript shows `Analysis Context (raw, pre-dedup): 161 of 262 findings are benchmark-synthetic`, then `Occurrence evidence gate removed 146 unsupported grouped occurrences`, then `Analysis Context (final report): 23 of 102 findings are benchmark-synthetic`. 262 - 146 = 116, not 102: 160 findings disappear and only 146 are labelled, leaving 14 dedupe merges unaccounted for. Metadata carries dedup_root_count=102 and dedup_occurrence_count=105 but no raw count and no merged count, and the integrity pass and noise cleanup emit no counters of their own.
gaps.actual_gap: OPEN, STRUCTURAL. Confirmed by artifact inspection: no metadata key records a raw finding count, a dedupe merge count, a gate removal count or an integrity-pass drop count. Not implemented this cycle because the console staleness (G-047) and the context-line population labelling had to be closed first, and adding a stage ledger touches every phase's reporting surface, which is a MED regression risk that deserves its own change rather than being folded into a repair.
gaps.implementation_location: main.py dedupe phase (raw/merged/gate/integrity counters), metadata key group alongside dedup_root_count, and the console stage ledger printed next to the Analysis Context lines

gaps.title: Executive insight counts disagree across console, JSON and PDF from one scan
gaps.problem: The same scan reports two different Critical/High totals in different deliverables. A human reading Security_Report.pdf and a downstream consumer parsing clean_report.json get different numbers for the same corpus, with no field saying which is authoritative. The severity table printed on the console and written to metadata.severity_distribution says High=4, while the HIGH RISK insight printed directly beneath it says 2.
gaps.reference_tool: Semgrep `--json` metrics vs SARIF counts, Trivy JSON vs table output, CodeQL `runs[].invocations` partial counts, SonarQube hotspots vs issues
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Render every summary from one computed structure and pass the population label alongside it, so a count cannot appear under two scopes in two artifacts without saying so.
gaps.current_behavior: Juice Shop, after G-047/G-048/G-049, one scan (372.8s, exit 0): metadata.severity_distribution = Critical 1 / High 4 / Medium 42 / Low 58 (scope SAST_findings_plus_unique_vulnerable_dependency_packages, severity_distribution_sast High 2), sast_findings 102 + sca_findings 3 = total_findings 105. Console SEVERITY DISTRIBUTION prints that same 105-row distribution, then INTELLIGENCE INSIGHTS prints 'HIGH RISK: 2 high-severity findings present'. clean_report.json `insights` carries the same 'HIGH RISK: 2' and 'COMPLIANCE RISK: 2 Critical/High findings'. Security_Report.pdf carries 'HIGH RISK: 2' but 'COMPLIANCE RISK: 5 Critical/High findings'. Three defects combine: (a) core/analyzer.py generate_insights counts the SAST-only population and emits prefix 'HIGH RISK:', so it never equals the combined table printed beside it; (b) reporting/report_mappings.py normalize_report_insights has a branch keyed on prefix 'HIGH SEVERITY:' which the producer no longer emits, so the HIGH RISK line is never reconciled in PDF/Excel either, while the COMPLIANCE RISK branch does fire and rewrites 2 to 5; (c) normalize_report_insights is called only from pdf_report.py and excel_report.py, never from the console path or from the JSON writer, so those two artifacts keep the raw producer text.
gaps.actual_gap: CLOSED this cycle. Root cause was three-fold: (a) generate_insights() counts the SAST-only population while the severity table and metadata.severity_distribution count SAST plus unique vulnerable dependency packages; (b) reporting/report_mappings.py normalize_report_insights() keyed on the prefix 'HIGH SEVERITY:' which the producer never emits, so the reconciliation never fired anywhere; (c) only pdf_report.py:1899 and excel_report.py:575 called it, leaving the console and clean_report.json raw. Fixes: added a 'HIGH RISK:' branch to normalize_report_insights(), applied it once at the serialization boundary in main.py after meta['severity_distribution'] = dist and before any consumer reads payload['insights'] (renderers re-applying it is idempotent, proven by test), and corrected the factually false contract comment in core/analyzer.py that asserted metadata.severity_distribution was built from the SAST population. New benchmark property P5 in analysis/benchmark_report_consistency.py measures severity-insight vs severity-table parity: P5 FAILED on the pre-fix artifact and PASSES on the post-fix artifact (5/5). Verified across all four artifacts from one scan: console HIGH RISK 4 / COMPLIANCE RISK 5, clean_report.json the same, Security_Report.pdf text-extracted the same. Fails open: a normaliser exception leaves insights in place rather than dropping them.
gaps.implementation_location: core/analyzer.py generate_insights (population qualifier and prefix), reporting/report_mappings.py normalize_report_insights (prefix pattern and call sites), main.py console insight printing and JSON insights writer so all four artifacts normalise identically

Cross-artifact delta 3. After (js_fix): console 'HIGH RISK: 4 high-severity findings present', 'COMPLIANCE RISK: 5 Critical/High findings'; clean_report.json identical; Security_Report.pdf pypdf text 'HIGH RISK: 4 ...', 'COMPLIANCE RISK: 5 Critical/High findings'. gaps.title: ATT&CK techniques present without tactics, version pinning, or detection mapping
gaps.problem: The product reports an ATT&CK table and users read it as ATT&CK coverage. What exists is 24 hardcoded technique-ID strings. There is no tactic model, no pinned ATT&CK version, no technique-to-detection/data-source mapping, and no measurement of how much of ATT&CK is covered, so 'MITRE ATT&CK coverage' cannot be answered with a number and several tactics the enterprise cares about are simply absent.

gaps.how_reference_does_it: Ship the ATT&CK STIX/JSON dataset with a pinned version, derive techniques/tactics/data-components from it rather than hardcoding IDs, and publish technique-to-detection mappings plus a coverage count against the dataset.
gaps.current_behavior: Measured this cycle on live source. 24 distinct technique-ID strings, all hardcoded: core/mapper.py:16-233 (14 rule entries), reporting/report_mappings.py:280-310 (MITRE_BY_RULE, 30 rule keys), core/analyzer.py:506-530 (11-ID description dict), analysis/ioc_malware_intelligence_engine.py:27-38 (12 regex patterns). Sub-techniques exist: exactly 5, only in analysis/ioc_malware_intelligence_engine.py:28,31,32,34,35. Absent, verified by zero-hit search: TA00xx tactic IDs and any 'tactic' field; Lateral Movement (T1021/T1210/T1570/T1550), Exfiltration (T1041/T1048/T1567/T1020/T1029), Impact (T1485/T1486/T1489/T1490), Resource Development (T1583-T1589), credential dumping T1003, T1036/T1070/T1562/T1564/T1055, T1136/T1098. No ATT&CK version string, no STIX, no bundled dataset, no attack.mitre.org or mitre/cti fetch (stix token count 0 recorded at docs/gap_analysis.md:1157). No technique-to-detection mapping: sigma 0 hits, log_source 0 hits; the 'detection' field is an engine provenance label (core/analyzer.py:419-449,534). Attack-graph edges are generic, not ATT&CK: core/graph_schema.py:13-18, and no T1xxx occurs in core/attack_graph.py. No coverage benchmark; the nearest thing is a staleness check (analysis/benchmark_report_consistency.py:184-206) and an aggregate test asserting ['T1083'] (tests/test_v11_report_boundary_consistency.py:99-109).
gaps.actual_gap: MEASURED_CLOSED, MINUS ONE RESIDUAL. Tactic attribution and version pinning were the two halves of this row that were genuinely open, and both are now resolved: every technique carries its kill-chain tactic(s), its ATT&CK status (CURRENT / DEPRECATED / REVOKED) and its attack.mitre.org URL, all from the pinned Enterprise bundle. RESIDUAL, DELIBERATELY OPEN: this tool still does not map ITS OWN detections to ATT&CK. The techniques on a finding are inherited from the rule that produced it; there is no systematic rule-to-technique table. The gap is that coverage of ATT&CK by this scanner is unmeasured, not that ATT&CK data is absent -- and measuring it honestly needs a labelled technique-to-control corpus, which this project does not have.

Stronger than first recorded: main.py:1316-1333 declares a dedicated output field `owasp_api_top10_2023` in `empty_list_fields`, and that field is present on 0 of 102 Juice Shop findings and 0 of 68 GenAI findings - so the API Security Top 10 has a *declared* slot that is never written, while the only API identifier anywhere is the string API4:2023 inside the generic `owasp` field, itself partly produced by the keyword fallback at core/analyzer.py:481. Web Top 10 and LLM Top 10 remain fully enumerated and per-rule (scanner/sast.py:84-277 declares cwe and owasp inline), and the LLM rule IDs are 2023-numbered while the emitted IDs are 2025-numbered with a correct crosswalk (LLM06_SENSITIVE_INFORMATION_DISCLOSURE -> LLM02:2025), plus owasp_id_2026 / owasp_llm_top10_2026 from core/owasp_mappings.py:243-244 citing the OWASP GenAI Crosswalk v4.0.0 / 2026-Q3. Field coverage is 100% on both corpora, but core/analyzer.py:482 unconditionally returns 'A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration' when every keyword test misses, so 100% coverage overstates mapping precision.

gaps.title: Regex is the detection technique for every language except Python; no parser exists for Java/JS/TS/Go/PHP/C#
gaps.problem: Language support is expressed as a `langs` list on each rule and several modules are named `java_semantic_*` and `java_taint_engine_v10`, which reads as semantic/AST analysis. The mechanism is a file-extension membership test plus `re.compile`. Python is the only language that reaches an AST. No benchmark stratifies precision or recall by language or by technique, so the class-A SAST F1=1.0 cannot be attributed to any particular path and the cost of the regex-only route is unknown in both directions.
gaps.reference_tool: CodeQL (AST + CFG + data-flow + call graph in a relational DB, QL/Datalog), Semgrep (pattern-AST vs code-AST, taint over an IL), Bandit (Python stdlib ast + node visitor), Brakeman (ruby_parser S-expressions + SexpProcessor), SpotBugs/Find-Sec-Bugs (JVM bytecode)
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Verified from each project's own docs and engine source rather than from reputation. CodeQL: extraction during the build captures 'syntactic data about the abstract syntax tree and semantic data about name binding and type information', producing a database holding 'a representation of the abstract syntax tree, the data flow graph, and the control flow graph', queried in QL (a Datalog dialect) where taint tracking extends data flow with steps that need not preserve value, and path queries are emitted with @kind path-problem. Semgrep: Match_patterns.ml visits the target AST, Pattern_vs_code.ml / Generic_vs_generic.ml compare pattern AST to code AST, and taint runs over an IL in Dataflow_tainting; --pro-intrafile adds interprocedural intra-file flow and --pro adds inter-file. Importantly Semgrep exposes regex as ONE of four explicitly named pattern classes (semgrep, spacegrep, aliengrep, regexp in Match_search_mode.ml) and its docs say string matching has been deprecated in favour of metavariable-regex - i.e. it segregates regex as a labelled fallback rather than using it as the primary mechanism. Bandit: 'processes each file, builds an AST from it, and runs appropriate plugins against the AST nodes' via BanditNodeVisitor, plugins declaring the node types they examine (@bandit.checks('Call')), with the documented limitation that the stdlib ast module only parses syntax valid for its own interpreter version. Brakeman: ruby_parser produces S-expressions consumed by SexpProcessor subclasses (BaseCheck < SexpProcessor) which track @has_user_input / @current_user_input across process_call/process_if. SpotBugs + Find Security Bugs: bytecode-level, works on compiled .class/.jar, and cannot scan source-only. The GitHub CodeQL team's own summary of the field is that 'the anatomy of most static code analysis tools can be summarized into three components: the parser, the internal representation, and the analysis of the representation' - R-SecOpsX has all three for Python and only the first (a regex match over text) for everything else, with no internal representation at all.
gaps.current_behavior: Measured over the 159 live .py files. Rule compilation: scanner/sast.py:286 `{**r, "pattern": re.compile(r["pat"], _F)}` - all 94 declarative rules become regex. Applicability: scanner/sast.py:1020-1023 `langs = rule.get("langs") or []; if langs and language not in langs: skip`, with language resolved by `def _language(path)` at :312, i.e. a file-extension test. Language dispatch in taint: scanner/taint_engine.py:2194-2198 `if lang == "python": _python_ast_findings(...)` / `elif lang == "java": _scan_java_semantic(...)` / then `_scan_enterprise_text(...)` unconditionally for every language, so JS, TS, Go, PHP, C#, Ruby and the rest receive only the text pass. The single AST entry point is scanner/taint_engine.py:11 `import ast` and :1785 `tree = ast.parse(source)`; Java's inputs are `_JAVA_SOURCE_PATTERNS` at :1831, a regex list. The Java modules are regex by import: scanner/java_semantic_j5.py:22-23 imports only `re` and `pathlib`; scanner/java_taint_engine_v10.py:21-22 imports only `pathlib` and `re`, with scan_j2/j3/j32/j32c/j4/r13 all accepting `source: str`. Technique census: regex 67 files / 654 call sites (taint_engine 128, java_semantic_j5 57, sast 34, secret_intelligence 31, llm_security 30, java_taint_engine_v10 27); `ast.*` only 7 files / 35 hits (aibom 8, idor_detector 6, taint_engine 6, abom* 13, undeclared_dependency_intelligence 2); config formats genuinely parsed - YAML 11 files/21 hits, JSON 25/38, XML 2/4; third-party parser libraries 0 - the one hit for tree-sitter/esprima/javalang is core/license_catalog.py:205 `"esprima": "BSD-2-Clause"`, a license name.
gaps.actual_gap: OPEN, now MEASURED. analysis/benchmark_language_granularity.py was added this cycle; it reuses the class-A corpus and the class-A `reconcile()` unchanged and only regroups the result by language, so it reconciles with reports/benchmark_reconciliation.json by construction (asserted as verdict v2, not assumed). Labels for each language's technique are re-verified against scanner/taint_engine.py at runtime (verdict v1), so the benchmark cannot report an 'AST' label after the dispatch stopped using an AST. RESULT on `sast-multilang-2026-10`: every language scores P=R=F1=1.0. AST (python, N=4) 4/0/0/5; REGEX java_semantic (N=3) 3/0/0/1; REGEX text-only (javascript, php, csharp, go; N=6 total) 6/0/0/0. Aggregate 13/0/0/6 matches the class-A benchmark exactly. Interpretation, stated so it cannot be over-read: this does NOT show the regex path is as good as an AST. Largest per-language denominator is 4 against a required 10 (verdict v4 FAIL), so the smallest recall step expressible is 0.25 for python, 0.33 for java, 0.5 for javascript/php and 1.0 for csharp/go - one miss would swing a language by 25 to 100 percentage points. The corpus simply cannot attribute a granularity cost either way. DECISION CONSEQUENCE: do not adopt a parser yet. The precondition for that decision is corpus depth, not code - raise each language to >=10 ground-truth vulnerabilities plus negative controls, re-run this benchmark, and only if a delta appears decide which language to parse first.

Precondition for choosing at all: raise each language to >=10 ground-truth vulnerabilities in analysis/benchmark_sast_corpus.GROUND_TRUTH so analysis/benchmark_language_granularity.py can return v4 PASS. Files that would change: scanner/sast.py:286 (rule compilation) and :1020-1023 plus :312 (language applicability); scanner/taint_engine.py:2194-2198 (dispatch), :1785 (the only ast.parse), :1831 (_JAVA_SOURCE_PATTERNS); scanner/java_semantic_j4.py, java_semantic_j5.py, scanner/java_taint_engine_v10.py.

Per-language (technique / GT / TP / FP / FN): python AST 4/4/0/0, java REGEX 3/3/0/0, javascript REGEX 2/2/0/0, php REGEX 2/2/0/0, csharp REGEX 1/1/0/0, go REGEX 1/1/0/0 - all F1=1.0. By technique: AST 4 GT / 4 TP; REGEX java_semantic 3 GT / 3 TP; REGEX text-only 6 GT / 6 TP. Class-A reconciliation 13/0/0/6, P=R=F1=1.0, identical to reports/benchmark_reconciliation.json. Source facts unchanged from registration: scanner/sast.py:286 compiles every rule with re.compile(r["pat"]); :1020-1023 gates on `language not in langs`; scanner/taint_engine.py:2194-2198 dispatches python->AST, java->_scan_java_semantic, everything else->text only; :1785 is the sole ast.parse; census over 159 live .py files regex 67/654, ast.* 7/35, third-party parser libs 0 (the lone esprima hit is core/license_catalog.py:205, a license name). Rule investment per language, measured by parsing the `langs` arrays in scanner/sast.py (78 rules carry an explicit langs list): java 36, csharp 22, javascript 19, typescript 19, go 15, php 15, python 10 (js and ts are usually co-declared, so the JS/TS block is 19 rules, not 38). This inverts the intuition behind the gap: python - the ONLY language with an AST - has the fewest declarative rules at 10, while java, the largest block at 36, runs on regex with five _apply_j{2,3,32c,4}/_r13 refinement layers stacked on top. C# (22) and JS/TS (19) get the text pass with NO semantic refinement layer at all. It also corrects a working assumption: csharp, not JS/TS, is the second largest rule block.

gaps.title: 14 business-logic pattern rules are built but never imported, so they never execute
gaps.problem: Business-logic abuse is an explicitly required capability, and a module holding 14 business-logic detection rules exists in the source tree. It is never imported by anything, so those rules cannot fire. The report still shows business-logic findings, which makes the gap invisible: they come from a different engine, so a reader sees 'business logic' coverage and cannot tell that half of it is inert.
gaps.reference_tool: Semgrep registry (every rule in a rule pack is loaded and can be counted), Nuclei template index (a template not loaded is not in the index), any engine with a rule registry that asserts rule count at startup
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Load rules through one registry and assert at startup that the number of registered rules equals the number on disk, so a rule file that is never imported fails a test instead of silently contributing nothing.
gaps.current_behavior: Import-reachability audit over the live tree (252 .py files, roots = main.py + tests/ + dump/ + runnable analysis tooling, following static imports, `from pkg import submodule`, relative imports and literal importlib/__import__ calls) reports scanner/business_logic_patterns.py as unreachable from every root. A repository-wide grep for the string `business_logic_patterns` returns zero hits outside the file itself - no static import, no literal dynamic import, no test. The module defines 14 rules: BL_SKIP_PAYMENT, BL_CLIENT_CONTROLLED_AMOUNT, BL_REFUND_APPROVAL_BYPASS, BL_NEGATIVE_BALANCE_ALLOWED, BL_MISSING_BALANCE_CHECK, BL_COUPON_MANIPULATION, BL_NEGATIVE_QUANTITY_ALLOWED, BL_ROLE_FROM_CLIENT, BL_APPROVAL_BYPASS, BL_IDEMPOTENCY_MISSING, BL_INVENTORY_RACE_CONDITION, BL_DOUBLE_SPEND_RISK, BL_LIMIT_BYPASS, BL_TRUSTED_CLIENT_STATUS. None of those 14 IDs appears in js_final/clean_report.json (102 findings) or genai_final/clean_report.json (68 findings) - measured, not assumed. Business-logic findings in those reports come instead from analysis/business_logic_correlation_engine.py, which emits a DISJOINT set (BL_PRIVILEGED_APPROVAL_GOVERNANCE_CHAIN, BL_PAYMENT_TAMPERING_CHAIN, BL_TENANT_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION_CHAIN, BL_WORKFLOW_BYPASS_AUDIT_GAP, BL_SENSITIVE_ROUTE_ABUSE_CHAIN, BL_MULTI_VECTOR_BUSINESS_LOGIC_CLUSTER) and is reachable - so the correlation half works while the pattern half never runs.
gaps.actual_gap: OPEN, and now correctly classified UNMEASURED rather than STRUCTURAL. Dry-run benchmark analysis/benchmark_business_logic_rules.py was built this cycle: it loads the rule table from either scanner/ or quarantine/scanner/ and applies the 14 regexes to the two corpora we already benchmark, WITHOUT modifying the product pipeline and WITHOUT adding a single finding to any report. RESULT: **0 of 14 rules exercised, 0 total matches across 746 source files.** The harness was proved to be reading those files, not silently skipping them: control patterns over the identical file set returned `req.` 664, `request.` 303, `price` 206 and `price =` 36. So the zero is a property of the patterns - they are narrow enough that even 36 `price =` assignments in the corpora none satisfy the request-derived shape BL_CLIENT_CONTROLLED_AMOUNT demands. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DECISION: wiring these rules in today would add ZERO findings to Juice Shop and GenAI, which makes the change look safe and successful while proving absolutely nothing about whether the rules are correct - it would be a change that cannot fail, and therefore cannot be validated. That is precisely the failure mode the project rules forbid. THE REAL PREREQUISITE is a labelled business-logic corpus: positive controls (a client-controlled price assignment that must be flagged) and negative controls (a server-computed price that must not), authored before the scan. Until that exists the choice between wiring and retiring is undecidable on evidence, so both options remain open and the module stays in quarantine.
gaps.implementation_location: PREREQUISITE: author a labelled business-logic corpus (positives + negative controls, written before the scan) - without it there is no target to move. THEN either restore quarantine/scanner/business_logic_patterns.py to scanner/, register it alongside scanner/sast.py ENTERPRISE_RULES (scanner/sast.py:83) and add a startup assertion that registered rule count == rule count on disk; or retire it explicitly and record that business-logic detection is correlation-only. Re-run analysis/benchmark_sast_corpus.py, analysis/benchmark_business_logic_rules.py and a full Juice Shop re-scan after any choice.
gaps.evidence: analysis/benchmark_business_logic_rules.py (new this cycle) verdicts: v1_rule_module_locatable PASS, v2_every_rule_exercised FAIL, exit 1. Measured: rules_exercised 0/14, total_matches 0, files_scanned 746 across D:\Data\Code test\prodtest\juice-shop-git and D:\Data\Code test\prodtest\GenAI-Red-Team-Lab-main; unexercised = all 14 (BL_SKIP_PAYMENT, BL_CLIENT_CONTROLLED_AMOUNT, BL_REFUND_APPROVAL_BYPASS, BL_NEGATIVE_BALANCE_ALLOWED, BL_MISSING_BALANCE_CHECK, BL_COUPON_MANIPULATION, BL_NEGATIVE_QUANTITY_ALLOWED, BL_ROLE_FROM_CLIENT, BL_APPROVAL_BYPASS, BL_IDEMPOTENCY_MISSING, BL_INVENTORY_RACE_CONDITION, BL_DOUBLE_SPEND_RISK, BL_LIMIT_BYPASS, BL_TRUSTED_CLIENT_STATUS). Harness control run over the identical file set: `req.` 664, `request.` 303, `price` 206, `amount` 36, `price =` 36, `refund` 0 - proving the walker reads files and that 0/14 is about pattern specificity, not a broken harness. gaps.title: mitre[] carries 7 tactics with a placeholder description and no dataset version
gaps.problem: Tactic coverage is a board-level metric. Rendering only observed tactics hides 8 tactics and implies coverage that was never measured, and a placeholder description is not tactic semantics.
gaps.reference_tool: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator; the Enterprise ATT&CK STIX dataset

gaps.actual_gap: MEASURED_CLOSED. The placeholder is gone. core/analyzer.py::_build_mitre_summary carried an 11-entry hardcoded table with the literal string 'Mapped ATT&CK technique' as the fallback for anything else, so T1595 shipped with that string as its description and both PDFs rendered it as a technique name. T1595 now resolves to 'Active Scanning' because the correct answer became available, and an identifier genuinely absent from the pinned bundle resolves to an EMPTY description with status UNRESOLVED -- the fallback was removed, not softened, because a fabricated name reads as an answer while a visible gap does not. Revoked and deprecated techniques are reported and flagged rather than dropped, so a report can say 'revoked' instead of implying the technique is current. MITRE_ATTACK moved from NOT_VERIFIED to VERIFIED, taking the mandatory baseline to 10 of 12.

gaps.title: No RBI FREE-AI traceability layer, though 12 of its recommendations have partial rules
gaps.problem: A regulated entity subject to the FREE-AI framework cannot ask whether a recommendation is met, because V11 carries no recommendation identifier on any finding or control.
gaps.reference_tool: RBI FREE-AI Committee Report (13 Aug 2025): 7 Sutras, 6 pillars, 26 recommendations; EU AI Act risk classes; NIST AI RMF
gaps.how_reference_does_it: Tags each control and finding with the recommendation or article it satisfies, so compliance status is a query over existing evidence rather than a separate exercise.
gaps.current_behavior: FREE-AI, RBI, Reserve Bank, sutra, IndiaAI, AI Kosh, NBFC and digital payment each return 0 hits across live code. There is no recommendation-number column anywhere. Substantively: Rec 23 AI inventory is strongly met (aibom 34, abom 25); Rec 24 audit is strongly met AI-agnostically (canonical_evidence, evidence_score, evidence_confidence, evidence_validation_detail, canonical_qualified_evidence, RCMSP decision_context/policy/outcome/provenance); Rec 15 data governance is partial-strong (DATA01-DATA05, DATA_TRAINING_DATA_LINEAGE_MISSING); third-party/vendor AI risk is partial-strong (COMP02-COMP05); Rec 14 board policy and risk classification is partial (COMP_AI_POLICY_MISSING, COMP_AI_RISK_ASSESSMENT_MISSING, COMP01_EU_AI_ACT_RISK_CLASS_MISSING); Rec 16 lifecycle governance is partial (GOV_MODEL_APPROVAL_MISSING, GOV_MODEL_OWNER_MISSING, GOV_MODEL_CARD_MISSING, GOV17_MODEL_DECOMMISSION_MISSING, REG04_MODEL_VERSION_DRIFT); Rec 20 red teaming is weak (GOV13_AI_RED_TEAM_EVIDENCE_MISSING and ADV_ADVERSARIAL_INPUT_UNTESTED detect the ABSENCE of red-team evidence rather than red-teaming); Sutra 4 fairness is weak for the same reason (GOV11/GOV12 detect absence, they do not measure bias); Sutra 2 human oversight is partial (GOV14_HUMAN_FALLBACK_MISSING, GOV_HUMAN_REVIEW_MISSING); Sutra 6 explainability is partial (COMP06_AI_EXPLAINABILITY_MISSING). ABSENT: Rec 21 BCP for AI systems (no model-degradation or fallback logic), Sutra 7 energy/sustainability (carbon and energy are 0 hits), Rec 18 consumer protection (0 hits), hallucination risk (0 hits). Also absent as vocabularies: NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, ISO 23894, OWASP AI Governance all 0 hits.
gaps.actual_gap: MEASURED_CLOSED. Recommendation-level traceability now exists: core/free_ai_mappings.py carries all 26 recommendations across the 6 pillars and all 7 Sutras, transcribed from the RBI's own publication page (ID 1306) and cross-checked against the KPMG India summary, which agreed on all 26 titles. Findings now carry free_ai_rec / free_ai_sutra attribution, so 'are we compliant with Rec 14, 19 or 20?' is answerable. TWO HONESTY CONSTRAINTS ARE THE SUBSTANCE OF THIS CLOSURE. First, 19 of the 26 recommendations ask for organisational acts a source scan cannot observe (form a standing committee, build an audit framework, build capacity), so they are classified NOT_ATTESTABLE_BY_A_SCANNER and only the 7 observable ones may carry a finding; free_ai_coverage publishes both denominators so a scanner can never appear to 'cover' FREE-AI. Second, FREE-AI is a COMMITTEE REPORT addressed to Indian financial-sector regulated entities, not a binding direction, and it does not automatically apply to an arbitrary codebase -- so every mapped finding carries free_ai_legal_status and free_ai_applicable_to_corpus=false. The 10 recommendations with no rule are recorded in FREE_AI_NO_RULE rather than left out of a ratio.

gaps.title: No SPDX exporter and no SLSA provenance; only CycloneDX and VEX are emitted
gaps.problem: Supply-chain acceptance criteria commonly require at least one of SPDX or CycloneDX (satisfied) plus machine-readable provenance. VEX alone does not satisfy SLSA-style provenance demands.
gaps.reference_tool: SPDX 3.x; SLSA provenance; in-toto attestations; CSAF 2.0
gaps.how_reference_does_it: SPDX as the alternative serialisation for a BOM; SLSA/in-toto as signed provenance for what was built and by which pipeline.
gaps.current_behavior: reporting/cyclonedx_export.py and reporting/vex_export.py are wired into main.py and confirmed by the cyclonedx_export and vex_export probes. There is no SPDX exporter: SPDX appears only as 6 vocabulary references, and no code path emits an .spdx document. CSAF is 0 hits. SLSA is 0 hits; in-toto has a single incidental mention.
gaps.actual_gap: MEASURED_OPEN, REDUCED. SPDX 2.3 is now emitted as Security_SPDX.spdx.json alongside CycloneDX and VEX, and the document is structurally validated against the pinned SPDX 2.3 rules BEFORE it is written, so an invalid document is refused rather than shipped. Three properties were treated as non-negotiable because the alternative is a false statement about what was analysed: filesAnalyzed is false on every package (R-SecOpsX reads a manifest and never unpacks a package), downloadLocation is NOASSERTION unless the payload carries a real URL (a synthesised registry URL would be a fabrication), and licenseConcluded is always NOASSERTION (the licence text was never reviewed). STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY: SLSA provenance / in-toto attestations. V11 is not the builder of the software it scans, so it cannot attest how that software was built; emitting an unattested provenance statement would be a counterfeit attestation. The SPDX creationInfo records the omission explicitly. CSAF remains absent (see G-083).
gaps.implementation_location: reporting/spdx_export.py (new); main.py (emits Security_SPDX.spdx.json); core/conformance_baseline.py (3 new SUPPLY_CHAIN probes: version pinned, dataLicense CC0, validated before write)
gaps.evidence: Built against the pinned SPDX 2.3 JSON schema (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spdx/spdx-spec/v2.3/schemas/spdx-schema.json), which declares additionalProperties:false at the document level and on every package -- so there is no place for a vendor extension block and every piece of V11 evidence travels in annotations, externalRefs or comment. Measured on the Juice Shop corpus: 168 packages, 168 DESCRIBES relationships, 0 validation problems, 168 unique SPDXIDs, and all 3 vulnerable components carry a VULNERABILITY EVIDENCE annotation naming their advisories, CVSS, EPSS, KEV and reachability. Two defects were found and fixed during verification: 162 of 168 components carry the literal string 'unknown' in their version slot because the manifests are unpinned, and emitting that as versionInfo fabricated a package identity (and collapsed 162 SPDXIDs onto one digest) -- versionInfo is now omitted with the fact recorded in the comment; and a package with only a CVE and no other enrichment produced NO annotation at all, hiding the one fact that mattered, so the primary advisory is now always named.
